verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Timothy the brother, to the church of God that is in Corinth, with all the saints who are in all of Achaia.
verses.1:2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation,
verses.1:4: who consoles us in all our affliction, so that we ourselves may also be able to console those who are in any distress, through the encouragement with which we ourselves are also encouraged by God.
verses.1:5: For just as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so also through Christ our consolation abounds.
verses.1:6: Now whether we are afflicted, it is for your encouragement and salvation; or whether we are consoled, it is for your consolation; or whether we are encouraged, it is for your encouragement and salvation, which produces endurance of the same sufferings that we also suffer,
verses.1:7: so that our hope for you may be firm, knowing that just as you are sharers in the sufferings, so you will also be in the consolation.
verses.1:8: For we do not want you to be unaware, brothers, concerning our affliction that happened in Asia, that we were weighed down beyond measure, beyond strength, so that we grew weary even of living.
verses.1:9: But we ourselves within ourselves had the verdict of death, so that we would not be trusting in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead,
verses.1:10: who rescued us from such great perils and delivers us, in whom we hope that He will yet rescue us,
verses.1:11: as you also help in prayer for us, so that from the persons of many, thanks may be given through many on our behalf for that gift which is in us.
verses.1:12: For our glory is this: the testimony of our conscience that in simplicity of heart and sincerity of God, and not in fleshly wisdom, but in the grace of God, we have conducted ourselves in this world, and more abundantly toward you.
verses.1:13: For we do not write other things to you than what you have read and understood. And I hope that you will understand even to the end,
verses.1:14: just as you have also understood us in part, that we are your glory, just as you also are ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:15: And with this confidence I wanted to come to you first, so that you might have a second grace,
verses.1:16: and to pass through you into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and to be escorted by you into Judea.
verses.1:17: Therefore, when I had wanted this, did I display fickleness? Or the things that I plan, do I plan according to the flesh, so that with me there should be "Yes" and "No"?
verses.1:18: But as God is faithful, our word, which was with you, does not have "Yes" and "No" in it.
verses.1:19: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you through us, through me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not "Yes" and "No," but "Yes" was in Him.
verses.1:20: For however many promises of God there are, in Him is "Yes"; therefore also through Him is "Amen" to God for our glory.
verses.1:21: Now He who confirms us with you in Christ, and who anointed us, is God,
verses.1:22: who also sealed us and gave the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts.
verses.1:23: Now I call God as witness upon my soul that, sparing you, I did not come again to Corinth;
verses.1:24: not that we exercise dominion over your faith, but we are helpers of your joy, for by faith you stand.
verses.2:1: But I resolved this very thing within myself, not to come to you again in sorrow.
verses.2:2: For if I make you sorrowful, then who is there to make me glad, except the one who is made sorrowful by me?
verses.2:3: And I wrote this very thing to you, so that when I come I may not have sorrow upon sorrow from those over whom I ought to have rejoiced, having confidence in all of you that my joy belongs to all of you.
verses.2:4: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you through many tears, not that you might be made sorrowful, but that you might know what love I have more abundantly toward you.
verses.2:5: Now if anyone has caused sorrow, he has not caused me sorrow, but in part, so that I may not burden all of you.
verses.2:6: Sufficient for such a one is this rebuke that comes from the majority,
verses.2:7: so that on the contrary you should rather forgive and console him, in order that such a one may not perhaps be swallowed up by excessive sorrow.
verses.2:8: For this reason I implore you to confirm love toward him.
verses.2:9: For to this end I also wrote, so that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.
verses.2:10: Now whomever you have forgiven anything, I also do; for what I too have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, has been for your sake in the person of Christ,
verses.2:11: so that we may not be outmaneuvered by Satan; for we are not unaware of his thoughts.
verses.2:12: Now when I had come to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and a door had been opened for me in the Lord,
verses.2:13: I had no rest for my spirit, because I did not find Titus my brother, but bidding them farewell, I set out for Macedonia.
verses.2:14: Now thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ Jesus and manifests the aroma of His knowledge through us in every place;
verses.2:15: for we are a pleasing aroma of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing:
verses.2:16: to some indeed an aroma of death to death, but to others an aroma of life to life. And for these things, who is so qualified?
verses.2:17: For we are not like very many, adulterating the word of God, but out of sincerity, but as from God, before God, we speak in Christ.
verses.3:1: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as some do, letters of commendation to you, or from you?
verses.3:2: You are our letter, written in our hearts, which is known and read by all people,
verses.3:3: made evident to be a letter of Christ, ministered by us, and written not with ink, but by the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets, but on fleshly tablets of the heart.
verses.3:4: Now we have such confidence through Christ toward God:
verses.3:5: not that we are sufficient to think anything from ourselves, as though out of ourselves; rather, our sufficiency is from God,
verses.3:6: who also made us qualified ministers of a new covenant, not by the letter, but by the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit makes alive.
verses.3:7: Now if the ministry of death, formed in letters on stones, was in glory, so that the sons of Israel could not gaze intently at the face of Moses because of the glory of his countenance, which is being done away with,
verses.3:8: how will the ministry of the Spirit not be even more in glory?
verses.3:9: For if the ministry of condemnation is glory, much more does the service of righteousness abound in glory.
verses.3:10: For not even what shone with splendor has been glorified in this respect, because of the surpassing glory.
verses.3:11: For if what is being done away with is through glory, much more is what remains in glory.
verses.3:12: Therefore, having such a hope, we exercise much confidence,
verses.3:13: and not as Moses placed a veil over his face, so that the sons of Israel would not gaze intently at the face of that which is being done away with,
verses.3:14: but their minds were dulled. For to this present day that same veil remains unlifted in the reading of the old covenant (because in Christ it is done away with),
verses.3:15: but to this present day, when Moses is read, a veil is placed over their heart.
verses.3:16: But when one turns to the Lord, the veil will be taken away.
verses.3:17: Now the Lord is the Spirit; and wherever the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
verses.3:18: But all of us, with unveiled face gazing at the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from splendor to splendor, as by the Spirit of the Lord.
verses.4:1: Therefore, having the ministry, just as we have obtained mercy, we do not grow faint,
verses.4:2: but we renounce the hidden things of disgrace, not walking in cunning, nor adulterating the word of God, but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every human conscience before God.
verses.4:3: And even if our gospel is covered, it is covered among those who are perishing,
verses.4:4: among whom the god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so that the illumination of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, may not shine upon them.
verses.4:5: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ our Lord, and ourselves as your servants through Jesus;
verses.4:6: because God, who said that light should shine out of darkness, has Himself shone in our hearts for the illumination of the knowledge of the radiance of God, in the face of Christ Jesus.
verses.4:7: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, so that the preeminence may be of the power of God, and not from us.
verses.4:8: In all things we suffer affliction, but we are not hemmed in; we are perplexed, but we are not left destitute;
verses.4:9: we suffer persecution, but we are not abandoned; we are thrown down, but we do not perish,
verses.4:10: always carrying around the dying of Jesus in our body, so that the life of Jesus also may be manifested in our bodies.
verses.4:11: For we who live are always handed over to death on account of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus also may be manifested in our mortal flesh.
verses.4:12: Thus death is at work in us, but life in you.
verses.4:13: Now having the same spirit of faith, just as it is written, "I believed, for which reason I spoke," we also believe, for which reason we also speak,
verses.4:14: knowing that He who raised Jesus will raise us also with Jesus, and will set us with you.
verses.4:15: For all things are on account of you, so that grace, abounding through many in thanksgiving, may abound to the glory of God.
verses.4:16: For this reason we do not grow faint; but even though our outward man is decaying, yet the one within is being renewed from day to day.
verses.4:17: For what is presently momentary and light in our affliction produces in us, beyond measure in sublimity, an eternal weight of glory,
verses.4:18: while we do not gaze at the things that are seen, but at the things that are not seen. For the things that are seen are temporary, whereas the things that are not seen are eternal.
verses.5:1: For we know that if our earthly house of this dwelling is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made by hand, eternal in the heavens.
verses.5:2: For indeed in this we groan, longing to be clothed over with our dwelling that is from heaven,
verses.5:3: if indeed we are found clothed, not naked.
verses.5:4: For indeed we who are in this tent groan, weighed down, because we do not want to be stripped, but to be clothed over, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
verses.5:5: Now He who fashions us for this very thing is God, who has given us the pledge of the Spirit.
verses.5:6: Therefore, being always bold, knowing that while we are in the body we are away from the Lord
verses.5:7: (for we walk by faith, and not by appearance);
verses.5:8: we are indeed bold, and we have a ready will rather to be away from the body and to be present with the Lord.
verses.5:9: And therefore we strive, whether absent or present, to please Him.
verses.5:10: For we must all be manifested before the tribunal of Christ, so that each one may receive back the things proper to the body, according to what he has done, whether good or evil.
verses.5:11: Knowing, therefore, the fear of the Lord, we persuade people, yet to God we are manifest. And I hope that we are manifest in your consciences as well.
verses.5:12: We are not commending ourselves to you again, but giving you an occasion to boast on our behalf, so that you may have a response for those who boast in outward appearance, and not in heart.
verses.5:13: For whether we are out of our mind, it is for God; or whether we are sober-minded, it is for you.
verses.5:14: For the love of Christ impels us, judging this: that if One died for all, then all died;
verses.5:15: and Christ died for all, so that those who live as well may no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again.
verses.5:16: Consequently, from now on we know no one according to the flesh. Even if we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we no longer know Him so.
verses.5:17: If, therefore, anyone is a new creature in Christ, the old things have passed away; look, all things have become new.
verses.5:18: And all things are from God, who has reconciled us to Himself through Christ and has given to us the ministry of reconciliation,
verses.5:19: since indeed God was in Christ, reconciling the world to Himself, not counting their offenses against them, and He placed in us the word of reconciliation.
verses.5:20: On behalf of Christ, therefore, we serve as ambassadors, as though God were exhorting through us. We plead on behalf of Christ: be reconciled to God.
verses.5:21: Him who did not know sin, He made to be sin for us, so that we might be made the righteousness of God in Him.
verses.6:1: And as helpers, we exhort you not to receive the grace of God in vain.
verses.6:2: For He says, "At an accepted time I heard you, and on the day of salvation I helped you." Look, now is the acceptable time; look, now is the day of salvation.
verses.6:3: Not giving any offense to anyone, so that our ministry may not be censured,
verses.6:4: but in all things let us present ourselves as ministers of God: in much endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,
verses.6:5: in beatings, in prisons, in riots, in labors, in vigils, in fastings,
verses.6:6: in chastity, in knowledge, in patience, in gentleness, in the Holy Spirit, in love without pretense,
verses.6:7: in the word of truth, in the power of God, through the weapons of righteousness on the right and on the left,
verses.6:8: through glory and dishonor, through bad reputation and good reputation; as deceivers, yet truthful; as those who are unknown, yet known;
verses.6:9: as dying, and look, we live; as disciplined, yet not put to death;
verses.6:10: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as needy, yet enriching many; as having nothing, yet possessing all things.
verses.6:11: Our mouth stands open to you, Corinthians; our heart has been opened wide.
verses.6:12: You are not constricted in us, but you are constricted in your own inward affections.
verses.6:13: Now having the same recompense (I speak as to children), be opened wide yourselves as well.
verses.6:14: Do not bear the yoke with unbelievers. For what sharing does righteousness have with iniquity? Or what companionship does light have with darkness?
verses.6:15: And what agreement does Christ have with Belial? Or what share does a believer have with an unbeliever?
verses.6:16: And what harmony does the temple of God have with idols? For you are the temple of the living God, just as God says: "I will dwell in them, and I will walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be a people to Me."
verses.6:17: "For this reason, come out from their midst and be separated," says the Lord, "and do not touch what is unclean,
verses.6:18: and I will receive you; and I will be a Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to Me," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.7:1: Therefore, having these promises, beloved, let us purify ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, completing sanctification in the fear of God.
verses.7:2: Make room for us. We have harmed no one, we have corrupted no one, we have defrauded no one.
verses.7:3: I do not speak for your condemnation, for we have said before that you are in our hearts to die together and to live together.
verses.7:4: I have great confidence toward you; I have great boasting on your behalf. I have been filled with comfort; I abound exceedingly with joy in all our affliction.
verses.7:5: For even when we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we suffered every affliction: outside, conflicts; inside, fears.
verses.7:6: But God, who comforts the humble, comforted us by the arrival of Titus.
verses.7:7: And not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you, reporting to us your longing, your weeping, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced even more.
verses.7:8: For although I grieved you in the letter, I do not regret it; even if I did regret it, seeing that (though for an hour) that letter grieved you,
verses.7:9: now I rejoice, not because you were grieved, but because you were grieved to repentance. For you were grieved toward God, so that you might suffer loss in nothing from us.
verses.7:10: For the sorrow that is according to God produces repentance to salvation that is steadfast, but the sorrow of the world produces death.
verses.7:11: For look at this very thing, your being grieved according to God: how much earnestness it produces in you; yes, defense; yes, indignation; yes, fear; yes, longing; yes, zeal; yes, avenging! In all things you have shown yourselves to be undefiled in the matter.
verses.7:12: Therefore, even though I wrote to you, it was not on account of the one who did the wrong, nor on account of the one who suffered it, but to make manifest our earnestness that we have for you
verses.7:13: before God; for this reason we have been comforted. Moreover, in our comfort we rejoiced all the more abundantly over the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you;
verses.7:14: and if I have boasted of anything before him about you, I have not been put to shame; rather, just as we spoke all things to you in truth, so also our boasting, which was to Titus, has become truth,
verses.7:15: and his inward affection is all the more abundant toward you as he recalls the obedience of all of you, how you received him with fear and trembling.
verses.7:16: I rejoice that in all things I am confident in you.
verses.8:1: Now, brothers, we make known to you the grace of God that was given in the churches of Macedonia:
verses.8:2: that in a great test of affliction there was an abundance of their joy, and their deepest poverty abounded into the riches of their simplicity;
verses.8:3: for according to their ability, I bear witness for them, and beyond their ability, they were willing of their own accord,
verses.8:4: with much urging imploring us for the grace and sharing of the ministry that is carried out for the saints.
verses.8:5: And not as we had hoped, but they gave their very selves first to the Lord, and then to us through the will of God,
verses.8:6: so that we asked Titus that, just as he began, so he would also complete in you this grace as well.
verses.8:7: But just as you abound in everything, in faith, and speech, and knowledge, and all earnestness, and moreover in your love toward us, may you also abound in this grace.
verses.8:8: I do not speak as one commanding, but through the earnestness of others proving also the good character of your love.
verses.8:9: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that on account of you He became poor, although He was rich, so that through His poverty you might be rich.
verses.8:10: And I give advice in this matter, for this is beneficial to you, who began not only to act, but also to be willing, from the previous year;
verses.8:11: now indeed complete it in action as well, so that just as the willing mind is ready, so it may also be ready to complete it out of what you have.
verses.8:12: For if the willingness is ready, it is accepted according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.
verses.8:13: For it is not that there should be relief for others and affliction for you, but out of equality.
verses.8:14: At the present time may your abundance supply their need, so that their abundance too may be a supply for your need, so that there may be equality, just as it is written:
verses.8:15: "The one who had much did not have too much, and the one who had little did not fall short."
verses.8:16: Now thanks to God, who put the same earnestness for you in the heart of Titus,
verses.8:17: for he indeed accepted the urging, yet being even more earnest, he set out to you of his own free will.
verses.8:18: We also sent along with him the brother whose praise is in the Gospel throughout all the churches;
verses.8:19: and not only that, but he was also appointed by the churches as the companion of our travels in this grace that is being administered by us for the glory of the Lord and our resolved will,
verses.8:20: avoiding this, so that no one may blame us in this fullness that is being administered by us.
verses.8:21: For we take care for what is good not only before God, but also before people.
verses.8:22: Now we also sent with them our brother, whom we have often proved in many things to be earnest, and now much more earnest through great confidence in you,
verses.8:23: whether regarding Titus, who is my partner and helper toward you, or our brothers, apostles of the churches, the glory of Christ.
verses.8:24: Therefore, show toward them the demonstration of your love and of our glory on your behalf, before the face of the churches.
verses.9:1: For regarding the ministry that is carried out for the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you.
verses.9:2: For I know your ready mind, on account of which I boast about you before the Macedonians that Achaia too has been ready since the past year; and your zeal has stirred up very many.
verses.9:3: But I have sent the brothers so that what we boast about you may not be made empty in this respect, so that (just as I said) you may be ready;
verses.9:4: otherwise, when Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we (not to say you) would be put to shame in this substance.
verses.9:5: Therefore I considered it necessary to ask the brothers to go ahead to you and prepare beforehand for this previously promised blessing to be ready in this way, as a blessing, not as greed.
verses.9:6: Now I say this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows in blessings will also reap from blessings.
verses.9:7: Each one, just as he has resolved in his heart, not out of sorrow or out of necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver.
verses.9:8: Moreover, God is able to make every grace abound in you, so that in all things, always having all sufficiency, you may abound in every good work,
verses.9:9: just as it is written: "He scattered, he gave to the poor; his righteousness remains forever and ever."
verses.9:10: Now He who supplies seed to the sower will also provide bread to eat, and will multiply your seed, and will increase the growth of the fruits of your righteousness,
verses.9:11: so that, enriched in all things, you may abound in all simplicity, which produces through us thanksgiving to God.
verses.9:12: For the ministry of this service not only supplies the things that are lacking to the saints, but also abounds through many thanksgivings in the Lord,
verses.9:13: through the proof of this ministry, glorifying God in the obedience of your confession to the Gospel of Christ, and in the simplicity of sharing with them and with all,
verses.9:14: and in their supplication for you, as they long for you because of the surpassing grace of God in you.
verses.9:15: Thanks to God for His inexpressible gift.
verses.10:1: Now I myself, Paul, implore you by the gentleness and moderation of Christ, I who am indeed lowly among you face to face, yet while absent am confident toward you.
verses.10:2: And I ask you that when present I may not be bold with that confidence by which I am thought to be bold against certain ones, who regard us as though we walk according to the flesh.
verses.10:3: For while walking in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
verses.10:4: For the weapons of our warfare are not fleshly, but powerful before God for the destruction of strongholds, destroying plans,
verses.10:5: and every height exalting itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing every understanding into captivity for obedience to Christ,
verses.10:6: and being in readiness to punish every disobedience, once your obedience has been fulfilled.
verses.10:7: Look at the things that are according to appearance. If anyone is confident in himself that he is Christ's, let him consider this again within himself: that just as he is Christ's, so also are we.
verses.10:8: For even if I should boast somewhat more about our authority, which the Lord gave us for building up and not for your destruction, I will not be ashamed.
verses.10:9: Yet so that I may not be thought as though to terrify you through letters:
verses.10:10: for indeed, "The letters," they say, "are weighty and strong, yet the bodily presence is weak, and the speech contemptible":
verses.10:11: let such a person consider this, that what we are in word through letters while absent, such we also are when present in deed.
verses.10:12: For we do not dare to rank or compare ourselves with certain ones who commend themselves; instead, we ourselves, measuring ourselves in ourselves and comparing ourselves with ourselves.
verses.10:13: Yet we will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the rule by which God has measured to us, a measure of reaching all the way to you.
verses.10:14: For we do not overextend ourselves as though not reaching to you, for we arrived all the way to you in the gospel of Christ.
verses.10:15: not boasting beyond measure in others' labors, yet having hope of your growing faith, to be magnified among you according to our rule to abundance,
verses.10:16: to preach the gospel even in those places that are beyond you, not to boast within another's rule in the things that have been prepared.
verses.10:17: Yet whoever boasts, let him boast in the Lord.
verses.10:18: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom God commends.
verses.11:1: If only you would bear with a little of my foolishness; indeed, bear with me as well.
verses.11:2: For I am jealous for you with the jealousy of God. For I have betrothed you to one husband, to present a chaste virgin to Christ.
verses.11:3: Yet I fear that, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his craftiness, so your minds may be corrupted and fall away from the simplicity that is in Christ.
verses.11:4: For if the one who comes preaches another Christ, whom we did not preach, or you receive another spirit, which you did not receive, or another gospel, which you did not accept, you would rightly endure it.
verses.11:5: For I consider that I have done nothing less than the great apostles.
verses.11:6: For even if I am unskilled in speech, yet not in knowledge, still in all things we have been made manifest to you.
verses.11:7: Or did I commit a sin, humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?
verses.11:8: I plundered other churches, receiving wages for your service.
verses.11:9: And when I was with you and was in need, I was burdensome to no one; for what was lacking to me, the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied; and in all things I kept myself without being a burden to you, and I will keep myself so.
verses.11:10: The truth of Christ is in me, that this boasting will not be broken in me in the regions of Achaia.
verses.11:11: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows.
verses.11:12: Yet what I am doing, I will also do, so that I may cut off the opportunity of those who desire an opportunity, so that in what they boast about, they may be found just as we also are.
verses.11:13: For such false apostles are deceitful workers, transforming themselves into apostles of Christ.
verses.11:14: And it is no wonder, for Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light.
verses.11:15: Therefore it is no great thing if his servants are transformed as servants of righteousness, whose end will be according to their own works.
verses.11:16: Again I say (let no one think me to be foolish; otherwise receive me as a foolish person, so that I too may boast a little),
verses.11:17: what I speak, I do not speak according to God, but as if in foolishness, in this basis of boasting.
verses.11:18: Since many boast according to the flesh, I also will boast.
verses.11:19: For you gladly put up with foolish people, since you yourselves are wise.
verses.11:20: For you bear with it if anyone brings you into slavery, if anyone devours, if anyone takes, if anyone exalts himself, if anyone strikes you in the face.
verses.11:21: I speak by way of disgrace, as though we have been weak in this respect. In whatever anyone dares (I speak in foolishness), I dare as well.
verses.11:22: They are Hebrews; so am I. They are Israelites; so am I. They are the seed of Abraham; so am I.
verses.11:23: They are servants of Christ (I speak as one less wise); I am more: in very many labors, in prisons more abundantly, in beatings beyond measure, in deaths frequently.
verses.11:24: From the Jews five times I received forty lashes minus one.
verses.11:25: Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I was in the depth of the sea,
verses.11:26: on journeys often, in dangers from rivers, dangers from bandits, dangers from my own people, dangers from the Gentiles, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false brothers,
verses.11:27: in labor and hardship, in many vigils, in hunger and thirst, in many fastings, in cold and nakedness,
verses.11:28: besides those things that are external, my daily pressure, the anxiety for all the churches.
verses.11:29: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?
verses.11:30: If it is necessary to boast, I will boast of the things that belong to my weakness.
verses.11:31: The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.
verses.11:32: In Damascus, the governor of the people of King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes in order to arrest me,
verses.11:33: and through a window I was let down in a basket down the wall, and thus I escaped his hands.
verses.12:1: If it is necessary to boast (it is indeed not profitable), yet I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
verses.12:2: I know a man in Christ fourteen years ago (whether in the body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know; God knows), such a one caught up all the way to the third heaven.
verses.12:3: And I know such a man (whether in the body or outside the body I do not know; God knows):
verses.12:4: that he was caught up into paradise and heard secret words, which it is not permitted for a man to speak.
verses.12:5: On behalf of such a one I will boast, yet on behalf of myself I will boast of nothing except in my weaknesses.
verses.12:6: For even if I should wish to boast, I will not be foolish, for I will speak the truth; yet I hold back, so that no one may reckon me above what he sees in me or anything he hears from me.
verses.12:7: And so that the greatness of the revelations may not exalt me, there was given to me a goad of my flesh, an angel of Satan, to buffet me.
verses.12:8: For this reason I begged the Lord three times that it might depart from me.
verses.12:9: And He said to me, "My grace suffices for you, for power is brought to perfection in weakness." Gladly therefore I will boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
verses.12:10: For this reason I am well pleased in my weaknesses, in insults, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ; for when I am weak, then I am powerful.
verses.12:11: I have become foolish; you compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you, for I was nothing less than those who are apostles beyond measure, even though I am nothing.
verses.12:12: Yet the signs of my apostleship were performed upon you in all patience, in signs and wonders and mighty deeds.
verses.12:13: For what is it in which you had less than the rest of the churches, except that I myself did not burden you? Forgive me this wrong.
verses.12:14: Look, this third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be burdensome to you. For I do not seek the things that are yours, but you. For children ought not to store up treasure for parents, but parents for children.
verses.12:15: Yet I will most gladly spend, and myself be spent beyond measure for your souls, even though, loving you more, I am loved less.
verses.12:16: Yet let it be so: I did not burden you; still, being crafty, I caught you by deceit.
verses.12:17: Did I take advantage of you through any of those whom I sent to you?
verses.12:18: I asked Titus, and I sent the brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Not in the same footsteps?
verses.12:19: Have you been thinking all this time that we are defending ourselves before you? Before God in Christ we speak; yet all things, most beloved, are for your building up.
verses.12:20: For I fear that perhaps when I come, I may not find you such as I wish, and I may be found by you such as you do not wish; that perhaps quarrels, jealousies, animosities, dissensions, slanders, whisperings, conceits, seditions may be among you;
verses.12:21: that again when I come, God may humble me before you, and I may mourn over many of those who sinned previously and have not repented over the impurity and fornication and shamelessness that they have practiced.
verses.13:1: Look, this third time I am coming to you: by the mouth of two or three witnesses every word will stand.
verses.13:2: I have said beforehand, and I say beforehand, as present, and now absent, to those who sinned before and to all the rest, that if I come again, I will not spare.
verses.13:3: Or do you seek proof of Him who speaks in me, Christ, who is not weak in you, but is powerful in you?
verses.13:4: For even though He was crucified out of weakness, yet He lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in Him, yet we will live with Him by the power of God in you.
verses.13:5: Test yourselves whether you are in the faith; prove yourselves. Or do you not know yourselves, that Christ Jesus is in you? Unless perhaps you are unapproved.
verses.13:6: But I hope that you will know that we are not unapproved.
verses.13:7: Now we pray to God that you may do nothing evil; not that we may appear approved, but that you may do what is good, while we may be as unapproved.
verses.13:8: For we cannot do anything against the truth, but for the truth.
verses.13:9: For we rejoice because we are weak, while you are powerful. This we also pray for: your completion.
verses.13:10: For this reason I am writing these things while absent, so that when present I may not act more severely, according to the authority that the Lord gave me for building up and not for destruction.
verses.13:11: Finally, brothers, rejoice, be perfect, be encouraged, be of the same mind, have peace, and the God of peace and love will be with you.
verses.13:12: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you.
verses.13:13: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with all of you. Amen.

notes.1:6: The Clementine Vulgate includes a third clause (sive exhortamur pro vestra exhortatione et salute) not found in most Greek manuscripts, and continues in 1:7 with a purpose clause (ut spes nostra firma sit) where the Greek has a coordinate statement ("and our hope is firm"). Throughout 1:3-7, the Vulgate alternates between consolatio/consolari ("consolation"/"console") and exhortatio/exhortari ("encouragement"/"encourage") for a single Greek word family.
notes.1:10: The Vulgate reads de tantis periculis ("from such great perils") where most Greek witnesses read "from so great a death"; et eruit ("and delivers") corresponds to a second Greek verb that many witnesses give in the future ("and will rescue").
notes.1:12: The Vulgate adds cordis ("of heart") to simplicitate ("simplicity") and uses gloria ("glory") here and in 1:14 where the Greek has kauchesis ("boast").
notes.1:20: The Clementine Vulgate reads ad gloriam nostram ("for our glory"), whereas the Greek reads "for glory through us." Earlier in 1:17, Latin Est et Non (literally "It is and No," the Vulgate idiom for "Yes and No") appears singly rather than the doubled Greek "Yes, yes and No, no."
notes.1:24: In the Latin text this verse is included in verse 23.
notes.2:3: The Clementine Vulgate reads tristitiam super tristitiam ("sorrow upon sorrow"), whereas most Greek manuscripts read simply "sorrow."
notes.2:5: In the Vulgate punctuation, omnes vos ("all of you") serves as the direct object of onerem ("so that I may not burden all of you"), whereas Greek editions often treat "not to be too severe" as parenthetical.
notes.2:10: Latin in persona Christi ("in the person of Christ") renders Greek en prosopo Christou ("in the presence/face of Christ").
notes.2:16: The Vulgate adds tam ("so") before idoneus ("qualified"), where the Greek asks simply "who is sufficient?" In 2:17, Latin adulterantes ("adulterating") renders Greek kapeleuontes ("peddling/huckstering").
notes.3:6: Latin non littera, sed Spiritu uses ablatives ("not by the letter, but by the Spirit") where the Greek has genitives.
notes.3:13: The Vulgate reads in faciem ejus, quod evacuatur ("at the face of that which is being done away with"), whereas the Greek reads "at the end of what is fading/abolished."
notes.3:16: Latin masculine singular conversus fuerit leaves the subject unexpressed ("one" or "he," echoing Moses in Exodus 34:34 or referring to Israel/any reader) and does not grammatically agree with neuter cor ("heart") in 3:15.
notes.3:18: The Vulgate shifts from gloriam ("glory") to a claritate in claritatem ("from splendor to splendor") where the Greek uses doxa throughout, and its genitive-ablative phrase a Domini Spiritu unambiguously means "by the Spirit of the Lord."
notes.4:4: The critical text capitalizes Deus; some ancient Latin interpreters joined hujus sæculi to infidelium ("God has blinded the minds of the unbelievers of this age"), while others read Deus hujus sæculi as "the god of this age."
notes.4:5: The Vulgate explicitly reads Dominum nostrum ("our Lord") where critical Greek texts have simply "Lord," and uses per Jesum ("through Jesus") rather than "for Jesus' sake" (contrast propter Jesum in 4:11).
notes.4:10: The Vulgate shifts from singular in corpore nostro ("in our body") to plural in corporibus nostris ("in our bodies"), whereas the Greek keeps the singular in both clauses.
notes.4:15: The Vulgate makes gratia abundans ("abounding grace") the subject of abundet ("may abound") with in gratiarum actione ("in thanksgiving") as a prepositional modifier, whereas the Greek makes thanksgiving the object or subject of abounding.
notes.4:17: The Vulgate reads in nobis ("in us") rather than the Greek "for us," and renders the emphatic Greek expression as supra modum in sublimitate ("beyond measure in sublimity").
notes.5:3: The Vulgate reads vestiti ("clothed"), aligning with the textual tradition "having put it on" rather than the variant "unclothed."
notes.5:7: Latin species literally denotes "visible appearance" or "form" (Greek eidos), contrasting outward visible reality with faith.
notes.5:10: The Vulgate reads propria corporis ("the things proper to the body"), reflecting an ancient textual variant rather than the standard Greek "the things done through the body."
notes.5:14: The Clementine Vulgate includes si ("if") in 5:14 ("if One died for all") and explicitly names Christus ("Christ") in 5:15, both absent from critical Greek texts.
notes.5:17: The Vulgate punctuates Si qua ergo in Christo nova creatura as a single conditional clause ("If, therefore, anyone is a new creature in Christ") and adds omnia ("all things") in the closing clause.
notes.6:1: The Vulgate renders the opening participle as Adjuvantes ("as helpers" or "assisting") without specifying an object, whereas the Greek means "working together."
notes.6:4: The Vulgate shifts to a hortatory subjunctive exhibeamus ("let us present") where the Greek continues with a participle ("commending").
notes.6:14: The Vulgate idiom Nolite jugum ducere ("Do not bear the yoke") omits the element "unequally" present in the Greek compound verb.
notes.6:16: The Clementine Vulgate reads second-person plural vos enim estis ("For you are") where critical Greek texts read first-person plural ("For we are").
notes.7:3: The Vulgate reads ad condemnationem vestram ("for your condemnation") and plural prædiximus ("we have said before"), whereas the Greek omits "your" and uses the singular "I have said before."
notes.7:8: The Vulgate uses the participle videns ("seeing") rather than a finite clause ("for I see"), linking this verse directly to nunc gaudeo ("now I rejoice") in 7:9.
notes.7:10: Vulgate stabilem ("steadfast" or "lasting") renders Greek ametameleton ("without regret"); grammatically it can modify either pœnitentiam ("steadfast repentance") or salutem ("lasting salvation").
notes.7:12: The Vulgate reads sollicitudinem nostram, quam habemus pro vobis ("our earnestness that we have for you"), whereas most Greek manuscripts read "your earnestness for us." The Clementine Vulgate also places coram Deo ("before God") at the start of 7:13 rather than the end of 7:12.
notes.8:2: The Vulgate supplies a separate verb fuit ("there was") for the first clause and renders Greek haplotes ("generosity / single-heartedness") literally as simplicitas ("simplicity"; likewise in 9:11 and 9:13), denoting ungrudging liberality.
notes.8:8: Vulgate ingenium bonum literally means "good character" or "good disposition," translating Greek gnesion ("genuineness").
notes.8:9: The Vulgate uses essetis ("might be") rather than "might become" (Greek ploutesete).
notes.8:21: The Vulgate reads coram Deo ("before God"), whereas most Greek manuscripts read "before the Lord" (enopion kyriou).
notes.8:24: Vulgate gloriæ ("glory") renders Greek kaucheseos ("boasting"), and in faciem ecclesiarum preserves the literal idiom "before the face of the churches."
notes.9:4: Vulgate in hac substantia ("in this substance") literally translates Greek en te hypostasei taute ("in this confidence / undertaking"); in Latin, substantia can denote either a basis of confidence or material means.
notes.9:6: Vulgate in benedictionibus ... de benedictionibus ("in blessings ... from blessings") preserves the literal biblical idiom for sowing and reaping bountifully.
notes.9:10: The Vulgate treats et panem ad manducandum præstabit ("will also provide bread to eat") as the first future main verb rather than part of the opening participle phrase, and expands Greek genemata ("harvest") into the double noun incrementa frugum ("the growth of the fruits").
notes.9:12: The Vulgate reads in Domino ("in the Lord"), whereas most Greek manuscripts read "to God" (to theo).
notes.10:2: Latin reads passive existimor ("I am thought"), whereas the Greek has middle logizomai ("I reckon" or "plan").
notes.10:10: Vulgate reads plural inquiunt ("they say"), whereas most Greek witnesses have singular phesin ("one says").
notes.10:12: Following the Western and Vulgate textual tradition, the Latin uses first-person plural pronouns ("we ourselves, measuring ourselves in ourselves") and omits the Greek clause "they are without understanding."
notes.10:18: Vulgate reads Deus ("God"), whereas the Greek reads ho Kyrios ("the Lord").
notes.11:1: Clementine Vulgate prints the infinitive supportare rather than the imperative supportate, translated here according to its hortatory sense ("bear with me as well").
notes.11:3: Vulgate adds et excidant ("and fall away") and reads in Christo ("in Christ"), without the Greek addition "and purity" found in some manuscripts.
notes.11:4: Vulgate reads alium Christum ("another Christ"), whereas the Greek reads allon Iesoun ("another Jesus").
notes.11:17: Vulgate reads secundum Deum ("according to God"), whereas the Greek reads kata Kyrion ("according to the Lord").
notes.11:23: Latin renders Greek paraphronon ("speaking like a madman") more softly as ut minus sapiens ("as one less wise").
notes.12:4: Latin translates Greek arreta ("unutterable" or "inexpressible") as arcana ("secret" or "hidden").
notes.12:7: Latin renders the Greek "thorn in the flesh" with a genitive phrase, stimulus carnis meae ("a goad of my flesh").
notes.12:9: Latin nam virtus in infirmitate perficitur omits the possessive "My" before "power" (matching older Greek witnesses) and renders dynamis as virtus ("power").
notes.12:17: Clementine Vulgate prints quod (for expected quos, "whom") referring back to eorum ("of those").
notes.12:21: Latin non egerunt poenitentiam literally means "have not done repentance," the standard Vulgate idiom for Greek metanoeo ("repent").
notes.13:2: Unlike the Greek text, which adds 'the second time' (to deuteron), the Clementine Vulgate reads simply 'as present, and now absent' (ut praesens, et nunc absens).
notes.13:3: The Vulgate opens a direct question with An ('Or do you seek...?') where the Greek has a causal clause (epei, 'since'), and uses in vobis ('in you') both here and in 13:4 where the Greek distinguishes eis hymas ('toward you') from en hymin ('in you').
notes.13:5: Verses 5-7 sustain a Latin wordplay on the root prob- (probate, 'prove'; probati, 'approved'; reprobi, 'unapproved'). The Vulgate also reads Christus Jesus ('Christ Jesus') here rather than 'Jesus Christ.'
notes.13:11: The Vulgate reverses the Greek order ('love and peace') to pacis et dilectionis ('of peace and love'). The imperative exhortamini renders Greek parakaleisthe in a passive sense ('be encouraged' or 'receive exhortation').
notes.13:13: Following the Vulgate verse division (which combines both greetings in 13:12, yielding 13 verses instead of 14), the benediction includes nostri ('our') and Amen, and translates Greek koinonia with communicatio ('communion' or 'sharing').
